notes.1: This question provided a welcoming start to the paper with the majority of candidates selecting the correct option. �PAGE�8
notes.3: Dichotomous keys were handled competently by nearly all candidates.
notes.5: This question required a quite detailed knowledge of the structure of xylem, which most candidates demonstrated.
notes.9: Many candidates showed a secure knowledge of the limiting factors for photosynthesis and many were able to correctly interpret the graphs.
notes.14: This question was based on one of the new topics (the effects of cholera) in the syllabus and the familiar but challenging topic of water potentials. Some candidates successfully selected the option.
notes.19: There was some confusion over the functioning of the heart valves for some candidates but many were able to select the correct option.
notes.22: There was a misconception among some candidates that an increase in the volume of the thorax produces an increase in pressure in the lungs.
notes.23: Some candidates were able to identify the correct option but many were less sure of how the oxygen debt is removed.
notes.26: That glucagon boosts blood sugar levels was reasonably well known: which organ produces it was less so.
notes.30: Many candidates knew which of the curves on the graph was the correct one for progesterone, but this question proved to be challenging for some.
notes.33: This was a challenging question, for some candidates, on two levels: understanding the terms hydrophyte and xerophyte and then applying the necessary biological knowledge. �PAGE�9
notes.general_comments:
Marks were very well spread across the mark range suggesting that all questions fell within the expected
capabilities of the candidates taking the paper. A few topics proved challenging for some and they were often
topics new to the syllabus.
